item.description: What can AI enable in medicine, and how do we get there? item.title: TokenEconomizer: Learning from Experience to Make AI Coding Agents More Efficient
item.dc:creator: Aaron J. Li, Weijia Xu, Chandan Singh, Jeevana Priya Inala, Bin Yu, Ion Stoica, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
item.description: AI coding agents can waste time and tokens relearning the same lessons. TokenEconomizer is an open-source plugin that builds on past sessions to cut costs while maintaining task success. It’s a path toward coding agents that learn not only how to solve tasks, but also how to spend computation more effectively. The post TokenEconomizer: Learning from Experience to Make AI Coding Agents More Efficient appeared first on Microsoft Research .

item.title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
item.dc:creator: Dimitris Papailiopoulos
item.description: Microsoft researchers have discovered “Lazarus,” a backdoor technique that can reprogram dormant neurons in an AI model, causing an otherwise normal AI agent to execute malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears. The threat is especially serious for AI agents with tool or terminal access. item.title: Formally verifying agent-written full-stack web apps with PDD Kit
item.dc:creator: Alex Lavaee, Matthai Philipose
item.description: AI agents can generate code at a scale that’s hard for humans to review line-by-line. PDD Kit helps ensure the code is doing what the developer intended by creating formal specifications and testing against them. It converts developer intent into a Verus specification, proves AI-generated code meets it for every input, and uses tests where proofs aren't practical. Developers review intent, not every line.
